levels.L1: Unit — pure Python logic in the API (e.g. onion/URL routing). No VM, no network, no app. Runs in milliseconds.
levels.L2: Integration — a real NixOS backend boots in a VM and its routing is checked over a transport. No app involved.
levels.L3: App usage — the SelfPrivacy app is driven like a user (open, navigate tabs, add a service, ...) against a running backend, and screen-recorded.

tests.name: onion URL routing
tests.desc: Unit-tests the API logic that rewrites service URLs for .onion path-routing (T1.1–T1.17).
tests.run:
# Pure unit test — no VM, no network, no target.
cd selfprivacy-api && nix run .#pytest-vm -- tests/test_onion_routing.py -q

tests.name: backend up + routing
tests.desc: Boots a NixOS backend in a VM and checks the API + nginx path routing are reachable over the transport (T2/T3).
tests.run:
# L2 integration: boots a NixOS backend in a throwaway test-VM and checks API + nginx path
# routing over the transport. No app, no real target.
cd Manager-Ubuntu-SelfPrivacy-Over-Tor/backend && nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.<L2-test>

installs.name: native · ethernet
installs.desc: NixOS installed directly on other hardware (laptop/Pi) over ethernet from this device. E2E: wipe+install+verify in one command (needs target booted in network mode).
installs.run:
# FULL end-to-end: wipe target disks -> install SelfPrivacy (NixOS) -> verify HTTPS from anywhere.
# Prereqs: your laptop on the TARGET's LAN (ethernet OR the target-router's wifi); target powered
#   on & reachable via SSH at IP; a deploy flake with nixosConfigurations.<host>; injected state/
#   extra (LE fullchain+key, secrets.json). The edge router must already forward :443 to the target
#   (one-off; see the openrouter 'selfprivacy-edge' branch).
IP=<TARGET_LAN_IP> MAC=<TARGET_NIC_MAC> KEY=~/.ssh/<DEPLOY_SSH_KEY> \
  DOMAIN=<YOUR_DOMAIN> TRANSPORT=https \
  FLAKE=<PATH_TO_DEPLOY_FLAKE> EXTRA=$FLAKE/state/extra \
  dev-dashboard/tools/e2e_install_native_ethernet.sh

# Verify-only (no wipe): does the running target serve the domain, trusted, from anywhere?
python3 dev-dashboard/tools/verify_install_native_ethernet.py \
  --transport https --domain <YOUR_DOMAIN> --token <API_TOKEN> [--ssh-key ~/.ssh/<KEY>]
# over Tor instead:  --transport onion --onion <56>.onion --token <API_TOKEN>  (needs tor SOCKS :9050)
